tpsa96:120: The view that "cross-cutting analysis is the real leverage point" deserves deep thought. Traditional project management is vertical—each team reports on its own matters, and managers make integrated judgments in their heads. This process has three problems: information attenuation (details are filtered when reporting), information lag (weekly reports are inherently delayed), and information silos (teams don't understand each other's dependencies).
